- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If model shows steady upward drift without recent price spikes, true outcome often reverses or corrects sharply — expect mean reversion in 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and continues upward; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment drops below 0.4, model tends to underestimate; add 2–5% upward adjustment to forecast if sentiment is falling.
- Model often overfits to recent history — if last 3–5 days are trending up, forecast may be too optimistic; cap forecast growth rate at 1.5x recent average daily change.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline after a spike, model may lag — adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in price correction.
- For 30-day horizon, if model is consistently above 95% of true outcome’s 30-day mean, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment history shows increasing volatility (e.g., alternating 0.7–0.9 and 0.1–0.3), model should not assume linear trend — apply stochastic smoothing or volatility-weighted adjustment.
